rationale: The predicate 'i=ruḥ-ayḏox azzá' means that the addressee's life is forfeited, matching sense 7 'hinsein, verloren'. The same predicate from the same supplied verse is already assigned to sense 7 in example 13 of this box. Sense 8 is 'weggehen, fortgehen'.

summary: File the hope-going-to-waste example under sense 7
rationale: The instance of ʔzl is 'u=amal diḏe əzzé b-am=maye', his hope going to waste, translated in the supplied verse as 'seine Hoffnung ... ins Wasser fallen'. data.turoyo: W gzayʕono aʕlux, ramḥəl d əzzux bu darbo d babux, məqṭolət.
data.translation: Und ich fürchte, du wirst Morgen denselben Weg gehen wie dein Vater und wirst getötet werden.

rationale: The father’s fatal path is echoed by bu darbawo at 29/210; one complete example illustrates the shared collocation.

summary: New idiom: azzé/əzzé m-bol- 'jdm. aus dem Sinn kommen, vergessen werden'

data.headword: azzé/əzzé m-bol- 'jdm. aus dem Sinn kommen, vergessen werden'
data.turoyo: Koḥozenux ġalabe zʕuro layəq šafiro. Kobaʕno d lo ʕəbrat hat bi masalaṯe, d lo haha məqṭolat w baḥ ḥayayḏi kulle lo kəzzux me boli!”
data.translation: Ich sehe, daß du ein sehr schmucker, schöner Jüngling bist; ich hätte lieber, daß du dich nicht auf diese Sache einließest, damit du ja nicht getötet wirst und du mein Leben lang mir nicht aus dem Sinn kommst!"

rationale: Fixed memory-source expression; search me boli found no duplicate, while ʔṯy lists the converse l-bol- recollection collocation. One ʔzl attestation.

summary: New idiom: əḏʕo l-ayko əzzé w-oṯe 'wissen, woran man ist, ein noch aus wissen'

data.headword: əḏʕo l-ayko əzzé w-oṯe 'wissen, woran man ist, ein noch aus wissen'
data.turoyo: Aw gyətwat, gmaqiminalan malko b dukṯux w aw gmoṭatlux ḥḏo, ḥatta d əḏʕina, laʔinnahu l ayko kəzzan w oṯina."
data.translation: Entweder du legst dein Amt nieder und wir setzen an deiner Stelle einen anderen König ein, oder du nimmst eine Frau, damit wir wissen, woran wir sind."

rationale: Knowledge clause plus paired going/coming, corroborated by the independent 115/272 parallel under ǧġl1; not a generalized conduct-business sense.

summary: New idiom: azzé/əzzé l-iḏe w-foṯe d- 'jdn. mit Hand und Gesicht begrüßen, sich versöhnen'

data.headword: azzé/əzzé l-iḏe w-foṯe d- 'jdn. mit Hand und Gesicht begrüßen, sich versöhnen'
data.turoyo: Komər mṭanne l ḥḏoḏe, mḥalaqqe a tloṯo abne du malko se Ḥasan w azzən l iḏe w foṯe d ḥḏoḏe, mṣalaḥḥe: "Aḥunoni hatu, xalaṣ, mede lo fayəš b lebi."
data.translation: Da versöhnten sie sie miteinander, sie brachten die drei Söhne des Königs zu Hasan. Sie gaben sich die Hand und küßten sich und schlossen Frieden." Ihr seid meine Brüder, " sprach er, "es ist vorbei, ich trage euch nichts nach."

rationale: Reconciliation supplies the greeting frame and the edition gives hands/kissing. Search iḏe w fo and l foṯ found no existing ʔzl collocation. One joint hand/face attestation, plus face-only 69/583; precise gestures queried.

summary: New idiom: (verneint) azzé iḏoṯo ʕal- 'Hände sind darüber gegangen (von der Bearbeitung eines Werkstücks)'

data.headword: (verneint) azzé iḏoṯo ʕal- 'Hände sind darüber gegangen (von der Bearbeitung eines Werkstücks)'
data.turoyo: Mamṭállalle, xəd kobəʕ. B ḥamšaḥṣar yawme mofaqle səǧǧade d əmmat: “Iḏoṯe l=azze aʕla.”
data.translation: Sie brachten ihm, was er verlangte. In fünfzehn Tagen brachteer einen Teppich heraus, daß man sagen möchte: "Es sind keine Händedarüber gegangen."

rationale: Craftsmanship formula with hands as subject and the crafted object as ʕal-goal. Search iḏoṯe and l=azze found no duplicate. Preserve the edition’s literal wording rather than infer a separate perfection meaning.

summary: New idiom: azzé/əzzé bəṯr xabro 'seinem gegebenen Wort folgen, es einhalten'

data.headword: azzé/əzzé bəṯr xabro 'seinem gegebenen Wort folgen, es einhalten'
data.turoyo: Walakən i=wəždanayḏi lə=kṭoʕən, ḥatta d ṭoreno mene, lazəm d əzzí bəṯre u=xabrayḏi.”
data.translation: Aber mein gewissen erträgt es nicht, daß ich ihn sitzen lasse; ich muß meinem gegebenen Wort nachgehen."

rationale: Possessed pledged word is the object of following; a commitment collocation. Searches bəṯre u=xabr and bəṯr u=xabr found no duplicate. One attestation.

summary: New idiom: əzzé zan d- ʕal- 'seine Vermutung fällt auf jdn. oder etw.'

data.headword: əzzé zan d- ʕal- 'seine Vermutung fällt auf jdn. oder etw.'
data.turoyo: L u goranawo hənnək ste gmətfakri w kul ḥa mənne ste, i naqqa d moyəd i šutke b iḏe, w u safrono, d əzzé zan diḏe aʕle, gdomalle. Gdomər: “Flan safruno yo.”
data.translation: Die anderen denken diesen Angaben entsprechend nach. Jeder von ihnen nimmt den Wollgurt in die Hand und nennt den Vogel, den er für den richtigen hält. Er sagt: "Es ist der und der Vogel."

rationale: Recurring possessed conjecture-subject plus ʕal-target at 94/440 and 94/457; light expression belongs here, distinct from desire I.5. Search zan di found no duplicate.

summary: New idiom: azzé/əzzé b-xaṭər d- 'sich mit einem Lebewohl von jdm. verabschieden'

data.headword: azzé/əzzé b-xaṭər d- 'sich mit einem Lebewohl von jdm. verabschieden'
data.turoyo: Hano, Nari, məllela li barṯo du malko d Məṣər, omər: "Hul šeṯ əšne bəṯre di masalaṯi no w kazzi b xaṭər diḏax!"
data.translation: Nari sprach zu der Königstochter von Kairo: Sechs Jahre werde ich hinter dieser Sache her sein, und jetzt gehe ich, leb wohl!

rationale: Attested departure plus leave-taking formula. Search b-xaṭ and b xaṭər found the bare farewell under ġrq but no equivalent ʔzl idiom; verbal collocation illustrated once.

summary: New idiom: azzé/əzzé b-oġur d- 'seinem Glück nachgehen'

summary: New idiom: əzzé xabro b-qarʕo l- 'ein Wort geht jdm. in den Kopf, jmd. begreift'

data.headword: əzzé xabro b-qarʕo l- 'ein Wort geht jdm. in den Kopf, jmd. begreift'
data.turoyo: Li kačke madʕalla aʕle, məlla: “Ašər, ʕaql du zlam našifo yo, xabro b qarʕe lo kəzzele, faqat ṭrowe hawxa!
data.translation: Das Mädchen antwortete ihm: Wahrlich, die Männer haben einen harten Kopf, sie begreifen nichts. Aber laß es nun so sein!

rationale: Cognitive motion with word subject, head as b-goal and -le affected person; search b qarʕ found no duplicate. One attestation; not desire I.5 or disappearance of faculties.

summary: New idiom: əzzé l-mirat 'ohne Nachkommen zugrunde gehen, herrenlos werden'

data.headword: əzzé l-mirat 'ohne Nachkommen zugrunde gehen, herrenlos werden'
data.turoyo: Ḥəlle, ḥəlle aʕli omər: "Way! Bayte d hanək, d hawxa səmme ebux, əzzeyo lu mirat!"
data.translation: Er schaute mich wieder lange an und sagte: „Oh mein Gott! Mögen die Leute, die dir das angetan haben, ohne Nachkommen zugrunde gehen“

rationale: Clear household-extinction result in a curse, specialized noun collocation under I.7. Search mirat found no existing entry. One attestation; exact property/heir force queried.

summary: New idiom: azzé/əzzé l-u rišo '(von einer Verbindung) gelingen, Bestand haben'

data.headword: azzé/əzzé l-u rišo '(von einer Verbindung) gelingen, Bestand haben'
data.turoyo: <...> W qayəm həwanwole i kačke, m darbe du admayḏe, lu abro du Gabro w bəṯər l azza lu rišo hayo stene w marfela. <...>
data.translation: <...> And then they had given the girl in compensation for his blood to Gabro's son, and afterwards that one too did not work out, and he let her go. <...>

rationale: Two reports (/961, /965) of the same marriage have negative lu rišo and subsequent separation. The fixed head-goal phrase differs from literal motion and confrontation; the permitted rišo search found no equivalent ʔzl collocation. Positive productivity and subject reference need confirmation.

summary: New idiom: əzzé w-oṯe ʕal- '(im Gespräch) immer wieder auf etw. zurückkommen'

data.headword: əzzé w-oṯe ʕal- '(im Gespräch) immer wieder auf etw. zurückkommen'

summary: The supplied routine counts strongly favour literal motion (Preterit Intransitive 3203, Infectum 1914, Imperativ 782). These are global sampled-input counts, not six independent batch totals.

Aspect: k- plus azzino/azzí can be immediately prospective in ko-Preterit. Past habitual əzze-/əzzən- with -wa belongs provisionally to Infectum-wa; coordinated verbs may share -wa. Do not assign tense from German past alone.

Dialect and speech: extended -hən, predicative-looking -yo, short 1sg -i, 2sg -ux and 2pl -oxu are attested. Repairs (azzan → azzi; azze → tre dayroye ... azzən) remain repairs, not new agreement rules. Female-speaker Azzino at Hors 2/133 is retained as a question.
The original JL 10.12.18 example is already correctly keyed I.7 in the supplied parsed entry. Repeated reader requests to change it from I.1 are based on stale metadata and cause no correction.

No experiencer-verb argument-coding or contact-language analysis follows from free translations alone. Heart/hand constructions have body-part subjects; noise has a recipient/affected hearer. Food, mediation and scalar frames are kept distinct from these participant extensions.

Batch 2 groups capacity for people and bushels as I.12, reciprocal visiting as I.13, involvement in a violent incident as I.14, and narrative continuation with bəṯr- as I.15. Earlier numbering 1–11 and all batch-1 additions remain.
The mtš entry explicitly contrasts present hič lo+kuzzí with kazzí. This supports caution over u-/ə-vocalized short forms; g- prospectivity and a short person ending alone do not prove ko-Preterit.
The frk II lookup includes an editorial/native reformulation of MAC Murder in Kfarze/133: be Xate azzehən (=qṭili). This is positive contextual support for death I.4, beyond the English went away.

Argument coding: -le/-la can resume a capacity container or a personal motion goal; do not make every l-suffix an agent. Goers remain subjects in the dog-goal and plural marriage-request clauses. New I.12 does not settle the grammatical alignment of all quantity/container tokens.

Batch 3 adds I.16 currency validity and I.17 confrontation, preserving 1–15. The finalizing meaning already exemplified under I.1 is clarified in its gloss. Inheritance transfer remains a note, and narrative focus 28/68 joins I.15.

Gender/number: some PrS feminine referents occur with Azze rather than Azza, and postposed coordinated or quantified subjects can occur with singular-looking forms. These observations do not establish gender-neutrality or a general agreement rule without recording/edition verification.

The detailed PrS 45/10 and 52/26 intended-action clauses strengthen the Preterit Intransitive I.3 box, while actual wandering remains I.1. A following activity verb alone is insufficient to classify every serial motion clause as ingressive.

The phrase identical to original ko-Preterit .3 is at supplied 6/58, so its citation is corrected. The exchange formula’s old prs 121/2 and current PrS 43/9 numbering needs editorial reconciliation; it is not silently replaced.

Batch 4 aspect: prospective Preterit Intransitive azzano/azzux in doom clauses coexists with prospective Infectum əzze/əzzeyo in death. Kazzalax describes completed absence at a habitual return; do not infer grammatical boxes from the edition’s tense alone.

Batch 5 morphology: a-vocalized kazzino is consistently ko-Preterit, while ə/u-vocalized kəzze/Kuzze is provisionally Infectum. Expanded azzayo repeatedly has explicit female human, ship and matter subjects, confirming it is not restricted to dying. Short gdəzzí/gdəzzúx/gdəzzín coexist with fuller forms; retain the printed accents and gender/person irregularities.

Batch 5 light expressions distinguish conjecture zan, promised word xabro, craftsmanship hands and greeting body-part goals from lebo desire. None warrants a new experiencer sense merely because the subject is abstract or a body part. No new Detransitive function is established by active mazlo in a go/come pair.

Batch 6 Detransitive mizəl is finite impersonal/modal in a sequence with mitamṭyo, unlike nominal mazlo in earlier batches. Together they do not establish passive or causative transport. summary: Moving images, propelled sandals/straw, flowing juice, information and noise retain motion/reaching with nonhuman or abstract subjects. No separate senses for each participant class.
Closure after a completed utterance or task is already present in PrS 121/2. The Lahdo repetitions corroborate it; successful completion is not automatically loss I.7.
M-adyawma azolo is temporal continuation, already included in the original idiom item at JL 19.6.18; do not duplicate it as a new idiom.
An affected possessor is suffixed (-li/-la) while lost cattle or children remain the subject. The free translation may instead make that possessor the subject of verlieren.
Measured liquid goes away during reduction; boiling is supplied by neighbouring predicates and must not enter the lexical gloss.
Flames, gas and illness may go away/cease without a new sense solely for the subject type.
A plough component or long bindweed can extend spatially; the Turoyo is not a distinct grow/extend verb merely because the subject is inanimate.
Procedural going can describe a repeated harvest action until the hand is full; this differs from the conventional bəṯra narrator questions now assigned I.15.
A village can go to a province in administrative affiliation. This is an abstract transfer extension; no physical movement or specialized bureaucratic verb is claimed.
Advancing in years (bann+əšne) is a variant of the original b-ʕumro age idiom, not a new idiom item.

evidence.cite: MAC NI Three kinds of death/4

summary: Removal of a tree’s inner material and loss of strength extend departure/cessation; a destruction sense is not forced from the subject alone.
News and letters go to recipients, including a recipient suffix on azzele. This is directed transmission without a causative or sending sense.

A house can go to an inheritance recipient/fisc; the verb supplies abstract transfer and the noun supplies the institutional setting. No specialized confiscation or inheritance meaning is inferred from German Fiscus.
Following a calf in a religious contrast and going along a thread are context-specific applications of following a target or path, not two further lexical senses.
Temporal Part act. variants m adyawma w azolo and m uʕdo w azolo belong with the already-listed onward idiom. No new participial sense is needed.

Flour, a road, radiance, murmuring, dust, a report and provisions are ordinary path/source/goal participant extensions. Food reaching l-riše is a recipient goal, not confrontational I.17. Literal hand motion in cramped space (paired with come) differs from unwilling iḏo I.5.
Work failing to go forward me qumayye is event progress; love directed l-riša is provisionally an abstract moving subject. The latter does not securely mean love rising to the experiencer’s own head.
The forward-time idiom has əzze, reduced ze and Part act. azolo variants; the original idiom already covers these, so I.6 and a new forward-time sense are unnecessary.
Head-loss oath, prospective doom, depleted life-force and vanished birds continue the loss sense; clauses about already dead birds need not be relabelled dying I.4.
Repeated negative b-gawe inability-to-bear clauses confirm the original idiom; allotted marriage at 61/5 confirms the naṣib collocation introduced in batch 2.

Firelight/smoke from a cave, a road by a pool, spreading news, a letter, good news and flies retain directed-motion semantics. Default agreement with household portions and extended -yo forms do not create senses.

Sleep not going to the eyes and another’s fatal path confirm the previously added sleep/fate collocations; no duplicate idiom example. Jumping farther/shorter and flying game pieces remain path/measure extensions, not separate jump/fly senses.

Matter continuing to the next year, indefinite future years and elapsed generations extend temporal participants. Forward continuation here has a matter subject and temporal endpoint, unlike the deictic from-now idiom.

Disappearing hair, wasted life, removed scoring heaps and missing belongings extend the lost/gone meaning. Life going into water confirms the original hope-in-water reassignment from I.5 to I.7; numerical quantity alone does not make a scalar-value I.10 use.

The soul-gone clauses occur as taunts to a cautious/frightened companion; the edition renders death from fear. Their status as imprecation versus mocking assertion is unresolved; no curse meaning is published.

Advanced-age b-əšne extends the original b-ʕumro idiom: human subjects, ʕumro subjects, short first-person azzi and Preterit-wa occur. This is distinct from numerical l-goal I.10 and elapsed-time I.6.
Additional age-subject numerical l-goals confirm scalar age in I.10. 111/92 is used analytically only because it has an alignment warning; unflagged 112/46 and 112/376 supply examples.
Ship fragments, fire/embers, a static cistern, a road, wrestling motion and sound remain participant/path extensions. Do not create burn, wrestle or cavity-layout senses from freer edition verbs.

Honour, grain, departed mental faculties, a lost chance and effort going into water continue established loss. Soul/heart/head subjects must be distinguished: losing reason differs from directed lebo desire and the word-entering-head cognition collocation.

Hand/face pledge gesture at 107/10 supports the earlier greeting collocation analytically, but its alignment warning prohibits an example. It differs from literal ʕal-hands/face landing (I.19) and crawling homage at 111/14.
The interview can go to the limits of a narrator's knowledge: new support for round-1 I.18, with epistemic rather than physical limits.
Commodity prices are expressed with b-amount or l-amount, supporting the numerical-value sense proposed in round 1; this is not the currency-validity sense I.16.
Large bottles hold litres and cupboards accommodate bottles; both continue round-1 capacity, with container-resuming l-suffixes.

Inquiry progress, route descriptions, bran displacement and smell-guided locomotion extend motion/path/manner participants. M harke w azolo and mə adyawma w azolo support the inherited onward formula.
Repeated əzzewo during a campaign describes temporal continuation; no separate impersonal sense is necessary. Bi ḥolo accompanies elapsed time, but its precise force remains open.
Memory loss and negative m hawno support the round-1 mental-loss and m-bol- forgetting discussion; money/books, grain and monastery property are participant extensions of loss.

Knowledge material personified as departing to the other world with its bearers and lice explicitly dying extend the death subject class. The pregnancy-loss euphemism is kept under I.7; broad death claims are not inferred from absence alone.

Mazlo remains in the inherited Detransitive Infinitiv and round-1 Detransitive sense 1, with ordinary active going meaning. Feminine məzəlto journey is not automatically assigned the same morphological box.
Sermon argument continuation with bəṯra supports round-1 I.15 in Preterit Intransitive; the reduced first-singular Azzi is retained.
M boli in negative date-memory and affirmative lost recollection confirms the round-1 forgetting collocation; bi hawa food-benefit loss confirms its labour-in-vain idiom.
Salon capacity is secure; broad cistern plus kuzzele maye is compatible with capacity but actual inflow cannot be excluded.
An explicit age of 110 years and a text running to five installments support round-1 numerical value/extent with additional participants.
Hostile action toward people with b hanək is followed by arrests and insults; supports the confrontation meaning with a b-target variant, whose productivity needs confirmation.
Bu zəyudo expresses going too far in the discussion, supporting the round-1 excess/degree meaning.

Guilt transfer, movable-fast cycles, periodical distribution, entering a broadcast or literary language, following a cause and money directed to a book extend participants, paths or purposes. No separate financial, technical or pursuit senses are introduced.
Illness cessation directly supports the round-1 I.8 participant extension; faith disappearing and community absence remain context-specific departures.
